main_text.p: quibus haud abfimilia, gaffer, gam-mer, pro good father, good mo-ther: buffe, pro bonfetwpfe; quæ familiariffimæ & ufitatiffimæ compellationes. Non minús autem contracta, fpittle, ex bofpitalle; oipin, ex auri pigmento; palfp, ex παρέλνυσ; parflp, ex petrofelynum; gourd, ex cucurbita. Talia Gallorum fouley, ex folifequium: & poulx, ex pediculus. Ex cujus ultimâ syllabâ (quod fateor non ordinarium, cùm terminatio non fit de essentiâ verborum) lonfe (vel ut alii lotofe) fufpicetur aliquis etiam Anglicum fluxiffe: nifi fit Latinum lues, Græcorum imitatione, quibus φθεῖρες, ἀπὸ τ φθογες. In plerisque contractis, aliqua etiam literarum tranfpofitio intervenit: quæ tanto magis obfcurat originem, ut in aridus, Dzp [?]: humidus, motst [?]: afper, sharp [?]: & fimilibus. Caterum quamvis in aliis non minús vulgaris, in propriis tamen, urbium præcipuè, locorumque quos hiftoria aut infignis aliquis eventus nobilitavit nominibus, magis obfervabilis contractio; ut Stambol, vel Sttmbotle, (quorum illud Turcis, hoc Græcis ufitatum tradunt:)

page.notes: Black letter words are set in a heavier face in the scan; marked with bl where the type differs. Several forms (buffe, dzp, motst, sharp, Sttmbotle, bofpitalle, lotofe) are hard to read and may be misprinted or misread; [?] marks the least certain. The Greek forms are copied as best read.
